title: Pullback preserves quasi-coherence on algebraic-space etale sites
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. The tensor pullback $f^*M=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}M$ of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], using the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], is quasi-coherent on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. No flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $f$ is required.

proof.text: Take quasicoherent local-presentation data P for M. Its scheme charts V_i cover the final sheaf of Y. By the chart-cover lemma the family of all q.left for q in A(f,V_i) covers the final sheaf of X. Use this family as the covering of the desired quasicoherent data.

For each pair (i,q), obtain the localized left adjoint F_q, the two left exact slice sheafifications, the structure-module isomorphism, and the natural restriction comparison. Left adjoints preserve all small colimits. Apply Mathlib SheafOfModules.Presentation.map to the given presentation P.presentation i and the structure-module isomorphism. Then apply Presentation.ofIsIso to the comparison at M, giving a presentation of (f^*M)|_(q.left). This transports both arbitrary small generator and relation types, using cokernels and no flatness.

The preceding family, covering proof and actual mapped presentations form SheafOfModules.QuasicoherentData for moduleTensorPullback f applied to M. Its isQuasicoherent theorem yields the required predicate, shrinking the covering index if necessary. The original theorem signature is unchanged.

proof_origin.place: Tag 03DO (lemma-local-pullback), proof, with Tag 03DF (lemma-global-pullback); source specialization spaces-properties.tex Tag 03GA. W3 makes the covering and chart-local tensor comparison explicit as two strict subsidiary lemmas and combines actual local presentations using Mathlib Presentation.map and Presentation.ofIsIso.
